en: The great thing about Ollama is that it has
a quite powerful
API that essentially allows you
to do pretty much everything you can do with
Ollama through the command line.
So for example, create models, list
available models, remove models.
You can do all these things
through their API as well.
And attached, you'll find a link to the API
documentation, which again is unfortunately
just a markdown file on GitHub.
But there you learned that you could also
create a model by sending a POST request to
the right endpoint.
You would have to specify a name for the
model
and then basically specify all the details
you would otherwise put into your model
file,
like the base model,
maybe a template,
parameters or messages,
or a system message.
So you could build a model programmatically.
And of course, for your own use on your
system, you might not wanna do that. Using a
model file and Ollama Create might be more
convenient.
But of course, if you're building some kind
of application which you wanna expose to
other users from all over the world and you
wanna automate the process of building
customized models, then this could be a
useful feature.
And it's not just that. You can really do
everything else as well, including deleting
or pulling models.
You can also generate vector embeddings,
which can be useful if you're building RAG
systems.
But you can, of course, also generate a
completion or a chat completion that takes
entire chat history into account.
And I got an example for that here. It's a
very simple Python script. And of course,
you find all that code attached.
And in that script, I send a request to that
/api/generate endpoint,
which is this endpoint here, to generate a
simple completion. So a simple output for a
received prompt.
Now this is sent to localhost:11434.
So that's the port
that Ollama uses for exposing the API.
That's the default port it uses. You could
change that with environment variables, but
by default, that is the port it will use.
And then here I'm configuring the request
data I'm sending along with the request,
specifically the model that should be used,
the prompt, and whether I want to stream
the result or just get it in one block.
And for the model name and the prompt text
here in this Python code, I simply have 2
parameters in this generate response
function.
And the concrete values for these parameters
are set down there.
So the model is essentially my Gemma 3
model,
but I could also use my service agent model
here, for example, that I have on my
machine.
So this model, which I created before,
and then here the prompt is hardcoded into
the file.
But of course, since this is Python,
I could also use the input function to ask
the user for input.
And now whenever I execute that file,
I would have to enter an input manually in
the command line and then that would be sent
to the model.
Well, and then all that's happening is that
a POST request is sent to that Ollama server
because a POST request is expected.
And then my prompt is handled by that AI
model
and the response is then parsed, returned by
this function.
And in the end, then
here
this response is being output.

text.

settings you can set when sending
such a request to the Ollama API
and more about the response format in the
official documentation, of course.

API file with Python,
I can ask, what's LM Studio?

prompt for
this model I'm using here, I actually told
it that it should not help with questions
related to
LM Studio.

it tells me that it's a friendly and helpful

3, 12B-IT-QAT, which is that base model
